small_body_encounter.support: Solar-heated activity creates a coma and connected tails; the dust tail may curve. The narrow authored geometry is retained without universalizing it.

stellar_lifecycle_observation.support: The original source depicts dust-obscured young stars, flattened disks and bipolar jets. Both lobes are not necessarily resolved in every cited view. Korean and English source rows keep the same narrow geometry.

galaxy_structure_observation.support: Gravity from close encounters creates tails, streams and shells. Existing paired-nucleus/bridge labels remain authored specializations; broader embedding alternatives are not contradictions.

compact_object_visualization.support: EHT describes a computationally interpreted radiolight shadow image. Source labels and aliases retain measurement/reconstruction context rather than claim a classical photograph.

solar_space_weather.support: NASA distinguishes electromagnetic flare flashes from ejected plasma/magnetic-field clouds. Existing source rows consistently select a coronagraph-mask and outward-front observation. KASI likewise explains an occulting disk as the coronagraph mechanism.

source_check_limits: This is bounded source consistency and name coverage, not validation of all astronomical physics or all space entries.
The narrower authored image specializations are preserved.
No official source is treated as proving rendered fidelity.
